newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean 3-yr yields end higher on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean 3-yr yields end higher on profit taking.

text.p: Yields on three-year corporates ended higher on Tuesday due to profit-taking after Monday's rally, brokers said.
"Securities houses seem to have become cautious after yesterday's strong sentiment. Profit taking emerged after the three-year yields hit a low of 11.82," said Park Ho-won, a broker at LG Securities.

Brokers said sentiment was boosted on Monday by hopes for a cut in the reserve requirement ratio. Brokers said the three-month CD yields also rose due to heavy new issues to a high of 12.20 in morning trading.
Brokers said new issues for the three-year corporates were estimated at 50 billion won on Wednesday, compared with 73 billion today.
The overnight call rates also edged up to 14.20 percent from 14.00 after Monday's fall.
